payload.summary: codex review round 3 (run s8rf125c, re-run directly because the dispatched session was filesystem read-only and could not write result.md): REQUEST CHANGES, one finding on the guard again. Every areas assertion matched only the HEADER row, so deleting the cards or rule row left the suite green while those named areas stopped existing and their elements fell back to implicit placement. Codex found it on the stacked block; the same hole was in both wide-width seat tests, which it had not been asked to check. Fixed with one expectHandAreas() helper asserting the complete three-row declaration, applied to all three sites. Four mutations — cards row and rule row deleted from the stacked block, cards row deleted from each wide seat — now all fail. Pattern worth keeping: three rounds, three findings, and every one of them was about the guard rather than the CSS. A CSS-text guard that matches a fragment of a declaration is worth roughly nothing.
